headline: Littler opens Grand Slam defence with win over Greaves
standfirst: The world number one averaged close to 110 in a 5-2 win in Wolverhampton as he chases a third straight Grand Slam title.
body: Luke Littler made a confident start to his Grand Slam of Darts title defence on Saturday night, beating Beau Greaves 5-2 in Group A at Aldersley Leisure Village.

The 19-year-old moved 3-0 ahead before Greaves, the Women's World Matchplay champion, began to find her range. Littler held her off to close out the best-of-nine-legs match with an average just below 110 and seven maximums.

The result extends Littler's unbeaten run at the Grand Slam to 15 matches. Having won the Eric Bristow Trophy in 2024 and 2025, he is trying to become only the third player, after Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen, to win three in a row.

It was a welcome performance after a difficult autumn by his standards, which included a quarter-final exit at last month's European Championship. Littler told BBC Sport he had been practising hard and was "glad I have shown it".

Elsewhere on the opening night, World Grand Prix champion Luke Humphries averaged 105.70 in a 5-3 win over Paolo Nebrida, and Gian van Veen posted 110.51 in beating Carl Sneyd 5-2. James Wade, Gerwyn Price and Chris Dobey also won their openers.
The tournament has been expanded this year, with 48 group matches across the first three days. Greaves meets Niels Zonneveld in her second group game on Sunday.
